question: Can a publicly indexed museum/voucher record be tied explicitly to Sanchez et al.'s 2023 Mandulog fish collection at Digkilaan, Upper Hinaplanon, or Bayug Island?

scope.study: Sanchez et al. 2024 article describing August-October 2023 fish collections at three Mandulog sites.
scope.matchRule: Count a record as linked only if its public metadata explicitly identifies the 2023 article, its author collection, or one of the article's named collection events/sites with a specimen/accession identifier. Same species elsewhere, historical Mandulog records, and unrelated records at place-name matches do not qualify.

searches.query: Reviewed the full study methods, Table 2 and linked publisher metadata for collection/voucher/accession references.
searches.result: The article describes collection by hired local fishers and expert verification but does not report a museum, voucher, catalog, accession, sequence, or specimen-to-name crosswalk.

queries: Bayug Island fish specimen collection Iligan
searches.result: No linked public fish voucher/catalog record surfaced in the returned results. Results were chiefly the publisher study or unrelated/locality-name material; search indexing is not an exhaustive catalog query.
searches.interpretation: Zero linked records in these accessible search results only; this does not establish that no voucher exists.

searches.result: The request timed out after 20 seconds in this environment. No response body or result count was obtained.

The API request could not be retrieved through the available web/API access in this environment; no query response or result count was obtained. The official portal notes that data stopped updating on 8 May 2026, while portal/API services were expected to remain operational through 2026.

The portal's own notice says its electronic data do not represent the full museum collection or all electronic/currently digitized specimen records. No complete or authoritative non-match inference can be made from this catalog alone.

excludedLeads: A publicly indexed 1938 botanical collection label mentioning the Mandulog system is not a fish specimen.
The 2013, 2014, and 2015 Mandulog fish studies are separate historical research and are not vouchers for the 2023 collection.
Fish records for the 14 names from elsewhere in the Philippines do not validate the Mandulog collection.

disposition.conclusion: No public voucher linkage was located in the accessible bounded search, and the two live occurrence/catalog API responses were not retrieved. The specimen-identity question remains unresolved; request the authors' specimen repository/accession list or repeat direct catalog queries when access is available.
